newsitem.title: UK: COFFEE OVERTAKES TEA IN UK DRINKS MARKET - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE OVERTAKES TEA IN UK DRINKS MARKET - REPORT.

text.p: Coffee has overtaken tea in the UK hot drinks market, according to a report published on Monday by Datamonitor, the market research group.
Coffee has grown at a rate of 11 percent a year since 1992, the survey said, and now accounts for the largest share of the UK hot drinks market.

British consumers now spend 15 pounds ($23.8) per capita on coffee each year, prompted by high profile advertising campaigns such as Nescafe's "Gold Blend" series, and a growing willingness to experiment with gourmet blends like espresso and cappuccino, said the Datamonitor report called "UK Hot Drinks 1997".
It also said the value of tea had declined to 691 pounds in 1997 from 726 million pounds in 1992 because the growth of own-label products had pushed down the price of brand-name teas.
